content: We don't stop playing because we grow old; we grow old because we stop playing.
author: George Bernard Shaw
sourceWork: George Bernard Shaw's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

George Bernard Shaw understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: What mental clutter or unrealistic expectation can you let go of to make room for simple joy?
